headline: New law orders a national study of child abuse, neglect, and deaths in youth residential programs, with recommendations for improvement.
what_it_does: The Department of Health and Human Services must pay the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine to study youth residential programs. The study will look at how common and how serious child abuse, neglect, and deaths are in these programs. It will also recommend ways to improve care and safety, and suggest training for workers who deal with these cases. The law itself does not set new rules for the programs.

who_it_affects.group: Children and teens in youth residential programs
who_it_affects.how: Their safety, care, and treatment will be the focus of the study and its recommendations.
Their programs will be studied, and the report may recommend best practices for them.

who_it_affects.group: Department of Health and Human Services
who_it_affects.how: It must contract with the National Academies to carry out the study.

who_it_affects.group: Health care, law enforcement, court, social work, and child protection workers
who_it_affects.how: The report must recommend education and training resources for people in these jobs.
The National Academies must consult with them while doing the study.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 23, 2024; the first report is due within three years, with follow-up reports every two years for 10 years.
